record.title: PASTABench reports weak optimal-timing performance in proactive agent-safety monitoring
record.summary: The authors introduce PASTABench, a paper-reported benchmark of 1,139 synthesized multi-turn agent trajectories across five risk categories and thirteen subcategories, with human-checked Earliest-Signal and Trigger turns defining an Optimal Intervention Window. In their evaluation of 16 language models, the paper reports that GPT-4o reached 40.74% Perfect timing and 68.22% On-Time interventions. The authors also report sensitivity to explicit hazard vocabulary in open-weight models. These are benchmark results on constructed trajectories, not evidence of deployed-agent safety or real-world harm reduction; independent reproduction remains open.
organizations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors published PASTABench, a benchmark of 1,139 synthesized multi-turn trajectories in five risk categories and thirteen subcategories.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the paper's evaluation of 16 language models, GPT-4o achieved 40.74% Perfect and 68.22% On-Time intervention timing under the authors' Optimal Intervention Window metric.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that neutralizing explicit hazard vocabulary substantially weakens proactive-safety results for some open-weight models in their benchmark.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The evaluated trajectories are synthesized and annotated benchmark scenarios; these results do not establish safety performance in live deployed agent workflows.

evidence_gaps.description: Independently reproduce the paper-reported metrics on the published benchmark and verify prompts, inference settings, sampling variability and artifact availability.
Test whether synthetic-trajectory results transfer to diverse live agent workflows and measured safety outcomes.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported intervention-timing and lexical-sensitivity failures generalize to agent monitors, they could materially change safety evaluation practice and deployment controls. The consequence is moderate because this is one paper's synthetic benchmark, without independent reproduction or evidence of real-world incident reduction.
limitations: The benchmark trajectories are synthesized with an LLM and span a bounded taxonomy; results do not measure live deployment safety.
Model rankings and timing metrics are authors' reported results and have not been independently reproduced here.
Evidence of lexical sensitivity in this benchmark does not establish that all open-weight models or safety systems fail similarly.

In their evaluation of 16 language models, the paper reports that GPT-4o reached 40.74% Perfect timing and 68.22% On-Time interventions. The authors also report sensitivity to explicit hazard vocabulary in open-weight models. These are benchmark results on constructed trajectories, not evidence of deployed-agent safety or real-world harm reduction; independent reproduction remains open.

technical.claimed_result: Across 16 evaluated language models on PASTABench, the authors report a best Perfect intervention-timing rate of 40.74% and identify lexical overfitting in some open-weight models after hazard vocabulary is neutralized.
technical.compute_or_cost: Not measured in the bounded source review.
technical.demonstrated_result: A public arXiv paper and benchmark description exist. The reported metrics and comparative behavior are paper claims; this activation did not independently reproduce them.
technical.implementation_status: Research benchmark and metric proposed in arXiv v1; production monitor implementation and live deployment impact are not established.
technical.mechanism: The authors define proactive monitoring along whether to intervene, when to intervene and what risk to attribute. The Optimal Intervention Window spans an annotated earliest observable precursor and a later trigger turn. The benchmark uses tool-mediated scenarios synthesized into evolving trajectories, then evaluates monitors' timing and risk attribution.
technical.novelty: The paper operationalizes intervention timing with an explicit window between first precursor and hazard trigger, evaluating proactive monitor behavior rather than only post-hoc trajectory verdicts.
technical.regime: Paper-reported evaluation on 1,139 synthesized multi-turn trajectories across five risk categories and thirteen subcategories, with human-checked temporal anchors.
technical.reproducibility: Independent reproduction and artifact inspection were not performed in this activation; inspect benchmark artifacts and repeatability analysis before extending the result beyond the paper-reported regime.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares 16 models under a common constructed benchmark and distinguishes Perfect from broader On-Time timing. It is not a deployment or incident-rate comparison.

brief.title: PASTABench reports weak optimal-timing performance in proactive agent-safety monitoring
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported benchmark behavior generalizes, agent monitors often fail to intervene at the useful point in a multi-step workflow, and surface hazard keywords may overstate some models' safety understanding. That would affect how agent safety is evaluated and deployed. The paper does not establish field performance, and its synthetic benchmark and model set bound the claim.
